data.body:
CRITERION: "state whether the two 2026-07-30 lease losses were genuine takeovers or spurious classifications — or, if no new occurrence has been captured, say so explicitly rather than closing on inference."

STATEMENT: **They cannot be classified, and no new occurrence has been captured.** Not
"probably spurious", not "probably genuine" — unknown, and unknowable from what exists.

The two events are Reconcile Bridge runs 30576272914 (2026-07-30T19:52Z) and
30579382013 (20:38Z), both aborting with:

    ref-lock renew: refs/reconciler/lock CAS rejected — lease lost/stolen
    ERROR: reconcile heartbeat lost the lease (pass_id=...) — aborting pass

Why they cannot be resolved retroactively: the branch that made the "lease
lost/stolen" claim raised WITHOUT logging the git stderr that justified it. The
evidence that would distinguish a genuine `stale info` lease mismatch from one of the
non-lease rejections this ticket fixed was discarded at the moment of the claim. It is
gone; no amount of re-reading the logs recovers it.

Circumstantial signals exist and are deliberately NOT being treated as an answer:
  * both landed ~86s into the pass, on the SECOND heartbeat tick (lease 120s,
    interval 40s) — an oddly precise coincidence for two independent events;
  * `renew`'s pre-CAS `read()` force-fetches from origin and saw the ref still at our
    own oid immediately before the push CAS failed;
  * no other run in the window logged a steal, and the workflow's
    `concurrency: reconcile-bridge` group serialises passes.
Those lean toward spurious. They are not proof, and this ticket does not claim they
are. Recording the lean explicitly so a future investigator has the thread without
mistaking it for a conclusion.

What this ticket's fix actually buys: the NEXT occurrence is diagnosable. The CAS
branch now logs the stderr, so the same question asked again will have an answer.

This criterion therefore closes as "explicitly stated, unresolved" — which is the
disposition the criterion itself names as acceptable ("or, if no new occurrence has
been captured, say so explicitly"). It does NOT close as resolved. If a lease loss
recurs with the new logging in place, the classification should be recorded here or on
a follow-up rather than the question being dropped.
